note: The three readers' answers and what confused them, as returned (Sonnet, fresh, frames only).

readers.q1: Pressing "Give the order" sends the ticked orders as one. Ney and Davout, the two ticked corps, each get "march to Lorraine" (2 actions each). Lannes is shown unticked, so he gets nothing. Soult is excluded because he is already at Lorraine.
readers.q2: It costs 4 actions out of the 4 in hand (2 corps at 2 actions each), which uses all of them. The top bar shows Actions 4/4, so you can afford it, but you would have none left afterward. No gold cost is shown.
readers.q3: Soult will not go, because he already stands at Lorraine. Lannes is also not going, but only because his box is unticked. He is not listed under "Will not go". Ney (and Lannes) carry a warning that they will drop the order for any battle within two provinces in a war of ours. That affects what they do later, not whether they go now.
readers.q4: Untick his box by clicking his row, or by using Up/Down to reach it and pressing Space. Davout's row is currently ticked, so one click would untick it.
readers.q5: Use "Take back" (Ctrl+Z), which is the button at the bottom of the map. The box says it undoes all the sent orders at once, so that would be the whole group (Ney and Davout's marches). I cannot tell from the screenshots whether it also refunds the 4 actions. I also cannot tell whether it reverses anything beyond this one batch.
readers.q6: Click the "Hold..." button in the "The Army of Italy — Lannes, Murat" box at the lower left of the map. The "Army of Italy · 2" chip in the left column selects those men. The log also says you can say "Army of Italy, hold". I cannot tell what the "..." on Hold opens (perhaps a choice of where or how). I also cannot tell whether Army of Italy has only Lannes and Murat, since the screen lists just those two.
